claims: "feature rich, sewing and quilting machine" and "perfect for larger quilting projects" (maker claims, Brother USA product page); no throat figure published
"Durable Metal Frame" appears in Walmart listing titles (listing claim); not on the Brother CS7000X page
"Perfect for beginners and experienced sewists alike" (retailer claim, qualitysewing.com)
"Sewed through eight layers of 12-ounce denim" (review-site claim, techgearlab.com); not independently checked here
conflicts: Throat space: the earlier claims row credited 'large needle-to-arm workspace' to the CS7000X page, but the Brother CP100X page carries that wording and the CS7000X page does not; the CS7000X page says only 'detachable wide table', so throatIn stays null.
Frame: Walmart listing titles say 'Durable Metal Frame', the Brother CS7000X page names no frame material (the 'durable metal frame construction' wording is on the CP100X page), so frame stays null.

Needle system: our earlier 130/705H value rests on manualslib only; Brother's operation manual and product page name needle sizes 65/9 to 100/16 but no system designation, so it is set to null as unverified.

Included feet: the Brother page 'In the Box' list says '10 sewing feet' but names nine feet plus a quilt guide, its spec table adds a 1/4 in foot, and the Brother operation manual sells the walking foot, quilting foot, 1/4 in piecing foot and quilting guide separately with the note 'Sold separately with some models'.
Free arm: the Brother page and manual say the free arm is available by removing the flat bed attachment, while some Reddit posters say the machine has no free arm.
Manual coverage: the Brother operation manual lists product codes 888-N00/N02/N20/N22/N40/N42/N60 and never names the CS7000X, so it is a shared-platform manual and its figures are platform-level.

Price: Brother USA shows $279.99 MSRP on 2026-10-02, the same figure as the Amazon third-party price tracked on 2026-09-18, against $302.49 comparable value at Best Buy and $219 reported by a PatternReview member.
Model naming: the CS7000X replaced the CS7000i; both are 70 stitch machines and used listings mix them. Specs here are for the X.

ownerThemes.theme: A sewing blogger's first impressions: easy threading, the automatic needle threader takes practice, and the wide table and drop feed make it workable for lap and baby quilts.
PatternReview members list the CS7000X around $219 as a second or first machine, and ask whether it is enough for bag making against the NQ900.

editorial.verdict: A budget computerized machine with 70 stitches, 7 one-step buttonholes and a wide table at $279.99 MSRP, but no published throat figure and a 750 spm ceiling.
editorial.whoFor: A first machine buyer who wants computerized stitch selection, an automatic needle threader and a drop feed for lap quilts at a low price.
editorial.skipIf: You need a stated throat in inches, speed above 750 spm, adjustable presser foot pressure, or a machine owners report as comfortable on thick layers.
editorial.keySpec: 70 stitches · 750 spm · 7 mm width · 7 buttonholes · 10.5 lb
strengths: Owners report quiet running and easy pedal control, per Amazon and Sewing Machines Plus reviewers.
Owners report several presser feet in the box, including an overcasting foot used for a faux serged edge.
Owners report consistent, even stitches, and the maker confirms drop feed and a free arm.
weaknesses: Owners report limits on thick materials, and one Amazon reviewer calls it not heavy duty for industrial level fabric.
Owners in help threads report defects such as the needle hitting the hook and a squeaking replacement unit; these threads over-represent problems.
Owners report threading trouble: a hidden take-up lever catch and unclear needle threader instructions.

faqs.q: Can the Brother CS7000X sew denim or canvas?
faqs.a: Brother's product page makes no thick-fabric claim. The shared manual lists denim of 12 ounces or more and canvas with a 100/16 needle, as general guidance rather than a layer count. Owners are split (4 positive and 5 negative statements on heavy fabric): one reports thick repairs and kimono mending without trouble, while a reviewer calls it not heavy duty for industrial level materials.

faqs.q: What is the price of the Brother CS7000X?
faqs.a: Brother USA shows a $279.99 MSRP (seen 2026-10-02), on the maker's own store rather than a dealer price. Prices drift weekly, so use the price band on this page as the stable guide.

faqs.q: Is the Brother CS7000X good for quilting?
faqs.a: It has a drop feed for free motion quilting and a detachable wide table that Brother calls perfect for larger quilting projects. No throat figure is published, and Brother's speed row is 750. One blogger's first impressions call it workable for lap and baby quilts.

faqs.q: What is the throat space on the Brother CS7000X?
faqs.a: Not published. The CS7000X page gives no inch figure and says only 'detachable wide table'. The phrase 'large needle-to-arm workspace' is on the CP100X page, not this one.

faqs.q: What feet come with the Brother CS7000X?
faqs.a: The Brother 'In the Box' list says 10 sewing feet but names nine feet plus a quilt guide, and the spec table adds a 1/4 in foot. The shared manual sells the walking foot, quilting foot, piecing foot and quilt guide separately with some models, so the count is soft. One owner found an overcasting foot among the accessories and used it for a faux serged edge.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Brother CS7000X and the CS7205?
faqs.a: On Brother's pages checked 2026-10-02, the CS7205 lists 205 built-in stitches, an 850 speed row, 8 buttonholes and $289.99, with the same stitch width (7) and length (5) rows. The CS7000X lists 70 stitches, a 750 speed row, 7 buttonholes and $279.99. The CS7205 page names a walking foot, a spring action quilting foot, a stitch guide foot and a 1/4 in foot among its feet.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Brother CS7000X and the XR9550?
faqs.a: On Brother's pages checked 2026-10-02, the XR9550 lists 165 built-in stitches including 55 alphanumeric, 8 buttonholes, a backlit LCD and $269.99, with a 1/2/25 year warranty split. The CS7000X lists 70 stitches, 7 buttonholes, an LCD with no brightness adjustment and $279.99.

faqs.q: What bobbins does the Brother CS7000X use?
faqs.a: Brother describes a Quick-Set drop-in top bobbin, and its manual says to open the bobbin cover and drop the bobbin in. One owner reports no bobbin winding problems after following the manual. The bobbin class is not published in the sources we hold, so check the manual or the bobbins in the box before buying a pack [verify].

faqs.q: How do you thread the Brother CS7000X, and does the needle threader work?
faqs.a: Brother lists an automatic needle threader and a Quick-Set drop-in top bobbin. Owner reports on threading are mixed (5 statements: 2 positive, 2 negative, 1 mixed): a sewing blogger found threading easy but says the needle threader takes practice, and owners mention a hidden take-up lever catch and unclear threader instructions. The manual covers the thread path, and we do not give steps here.
